groups.writingJob: Build every non-particle vocable as a complete nuclear clause with a subject and a predicate, and allow that clause to serve as a sentence, main clause, dependent clause, or conjoined clause.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recognize a nuclear clause as a clause rather than an English-style word and recover its subject and predicate.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the intended content and construction; the application keeps non-particles inside nuclear-clause structure and supplies the required subject-predicate frame.

groups.title: The basic subject-predicate formula

groups.title: VNC and NNC structure and hierarchy
groups.proposal: Make VNC and NNC formulas direct views of the same typed structure that builds the Result.
groups.writingJob: Build the discontinuous subject around the predicate; build NNC predicates from state and nounstem; build VNC predicates from valence, verbstem, and tense; preserve every layer of the hierarchy.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recover the subject, core, predicate, state, valence, tense, and stem-centered hierarchy from a completed form.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses applicable grammatical meanings; the application orders and joins the corresponding constituents and derives the formula hierarchy.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse person, number, state, valence, tense, and source controls. Do not expose constituent order, circumfix assembly, hierarchy, or formula boundaries as choices.

groups.title: The six VNC and NNC formula shapes
groups.proposal: Make formula selection an automatic result of the active VNC or NNC grammar, never a display-only label.
groups.writingJob: Select the correct VNC or NNC formula automatically from dyadic, monadic, or vacant valence or state, while preserving dyadic person and number, monadic tense, and an open stem structure.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader identify the active formula, its subpositions, and why an implicit valence or state may be absent from the written formula.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the grammatical construction and needed participants; the application derives which of the six formula shapes applies.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add a formula-number picker. State and valence controls may express genuine choices, but dyadic, monadic, or vacant shape is derived from them.

groups.title: Personal pronouns and reference
groups.proposal: Make the five pronoun categories govern normal VNC and NNC behavior while keeping contextual interpretation in the reading guide.
groups.writingJob: Build personal pronouns only as affixes in the authorized person, number, objective, and possessive positions; preserve person, animacy, humanness, number, and case; leave contextual reference and English gender to interpretation.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through affixal pronouns, third-person ambiguity, common number, cultural animacy, case, deixis, anaphora, and cataphora.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intended participants and any context the application truly needs; the application selects and places pronoun forms, enforces case and clause compatibility, and never invents an English gender distinction.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse participant, person, number, animacy, humanness, object, possessor, and context choices only when they change grammar or meaning. Do not add gender, deixis terminology, or anaphora terminology as required controls.
